Welwyn Hatfield's population increased by around 9,300 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 120,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Welwyn Hatfield increased by 8.4%, from around 110,500 in 2011 to around 119,800 in 2021.

The population here increased at a similar rate to the overall population of the East of England (8.3%), but by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Welwyn Hatfield was home to around 6.6 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 6.1 in 2011. This area was close to the median population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was similar in Welwyn Hatfield to the East of England as a whole

Median age in Welwyn Hatfield

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Welwyn Hatfield increased by one year, from 36 to 37 years of age.

This area had a lower average (median) age than the East of England as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just under 3,600 (an increase of 19.9%), while the number of residents between 20 and 24 years fell by just over 850 (7.5% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.7 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Employment in Welwyn Hatfield

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed increased in Welwyn Hatfield, but fell across the East of England.

In Welwyn Hatfield, the percentage who were employed rose from 54.5% in 2011 to 56.0% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 58.4% to 57.3%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Welwyn Hatfield fell from 3.0% to 2.4%, while the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were retired (economically inactive) decreased from 18.9% to 17.9%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Welwyn Hatfield increased by 1.5 percentage points

Welwyn Hatfield stood out from other areas for working hours

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week fell here, but rose across the East of England.

In Welwyn Hatfield, the percentage that worked 15 hours or less in a week fell from 12.2% in 2011 to 11.6% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 10.4% to 10.8%.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in Welwyn Hatfield fell from 13.1% to 11.1%, while the percentage of adults in employment who worked 31 to 48 hours increased from 56.9% to 59.2%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Welwyn Hatfield decreased by 0.5 percentage points

Family in Welwyn Hatfield

Welwyn Hatfield saw the East of England's second-largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of households including a couple with only non-dependent children (from 5.9% in 2011 to 6.9% in 2021).

Across the region, only Three Rivers saw a greater rise in the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children (from 7.4% to 8.4%).

Across the East of England, the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children increased from 6.4% to 6.6%, while the percentage in nearby East Hertfordshire increased from 6.4% to 7.2%.

The percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children in Welwyn Hatfield increased by 1.0 percentage points

Change in housing in Welwyn Hatfield

Of Welwyn Hatfield households, 56.6% owned their home in 2021, down from 57.3% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in six households (16.4%) rented privately, compared with 13.6% in 2011. The percentage of Welwyn Hatfield households that lived in a socially rented property decreased from 26.9% to 25.4%.

The decrease in the percentage of households that owned their home was greater across the East of England (2.4 percentage points, from 67.6% to 65.2%) than in Welwyn Hatfield (0.7 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.0 percentage points, from 63.3% to 61.3%.

The rate of home ownership in Welwyn Hatfield decreased by 0.7 percentage points

Welwyn Hatfield residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 91,000 Welwyn Hatfield residents said they were born in England. This represented 75.9% of the local population. The figure has risen from just under 88,500 in 2011, which at the time represented 80.1% of Welwyn Hatfield's population.

India was the next most represented, with around 2,800 Welwyn Hatfield residents reporting this country of birth (2.4%). This figure was up from just under 1,900 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.7% of the population of Welwyn Hatfield.

The number of Welwyn Hatfield residents born in Romania rose from around 200 in 2011 (0.2% of the local population) to around 2,700 in 2021 (2.3%).

In 2021, 75.9% of Welwyn Hatfield residents reported their country of birth as England

Unpaid care in Welwyn Hatfield

In 2021, 4.7% of Welwyn Hatfield residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.5% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.6% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.2% in 2011. The proportion of Welwyn Hatfield residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care remained at 2.3%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Welwyn Hatfield (2.8 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the East of England (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Welwyn Hatfield decreased by 2.8 percentage points

Religion in Welwyn Hatfield

In 2021, 37.0% of Welwyn Hatfield residents reported having "No religion", up from 27.9% in 2011. The rise of 9.1 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Welwyn Hatfield. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the East of England, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.9% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 47.2% of people in Welwyn Hatfield described themselves as Christian (down from 57.5%), while 6.7% did not state their religion (down from 7.1% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

National identity in Welwyn Hatfield

In 2021, 13.2% of Welwyn Hatfield residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 11.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 40 people (2.7%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 1.2% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Welwyn Hatfield that identified as "British only" increased from 18.1% to 54.7%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the East of England (2.1 percentage points, from 6.9% to 9.0%) than in Welwyn Hatfield (1.6 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Welwyn Hatfield increased by 1.6 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Welwyn Hatfield residents aged 16 years and over, 40.9% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 38.7% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 4 in 10 people (43.6%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 44.7% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Welwyn Hatfield that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 7.8% to 8.0%.

This area had the region’s third highest percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership. Across the region, only Cambridge (56.5%) and Norwich (52.4%) had a higher percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Welwyn Hatfield increased by 2.2 percentage points

Disability in Welwyn Hatfield

In 2021, 6.0% of Welwyn Hatfield residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 7.1% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 10 people (9.7%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.2% in 2011. The proportion of Welwyn Hatfield residents who were not disabled increased from 83.6% to 84.2%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Welwyn Hatfield (1.1 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the East of England (1.2 percentage points, from 7.8% to 6.6%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Welwyn Hatfield decreased by 1.1 percentage points

Health in Welwyn Hatfield

In 2021, 49.3% of Welwyn Hatfield residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 47.6% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 35.2% to 34.6%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Welwyn Hatfield residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.9% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.6% to 3.4%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Welwyn Hatfield increased by 1.7 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Welwyn Hatfield

In 2021, 6.1% of Welwyn Hatfield residents identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category, up from 4.5% in 2011. The 1.6 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the East of England, the percentage of people from the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" ethnic group increased from 2.0% to 2.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 3.5% to 4.2%.

In 2021, 78.7% of people in Welwyn Hatfield identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 84.1% in 2011), while 8.8% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 7.9% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category increased from 2.5% in 2011 to 4.1% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
